newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast McMahon gas plant in partial outage.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast McMahon gas plant in partial outage.

text.p: An unscheduled outage that started on Saturday at Westcoast Energy Inc's McMahon gas plant in northeast British Columbia is expected to last another four to seven days, a Westcoast spokesman said on Tuesday.
The company declared a force majeure following a partial shutdown because of mechanical problems at the facility, which has a capacity of nearly 700 million cubic feet of gas per day.
"It's affecting only some interruptible customers. All the firm (customers) are locked in," the spokesman said.
He said estimates issued on October 12 for the length of time repairs would take were seven to 10 days.
The plant was processing 530 million cubic feet of gas per day on Tuesday and was expected to run at 560 MMCFD on Wednesday and 640 MMCFD on Thursday, he said.
Traders on Tuesday said the partial outage played a big role in a jump in gas prices at the Huntington/Sumas border point following Canada's Thanksgiving Day holiday on Monday.
Sumas gas was quoted at US$1.08/1.12 per million British thermal units, up from a notional US$0.96/0.91 on Monday.
